---
title: "Day 9 — Make a report that runs its own calculations"
---

## Today's question

Can someone read our explanation, inspect our calculation, and see the figure
without copying results manually? An **R Markdown report** combines ordinary text
with executable R code. Rendering turns that source document into a readable HTML
report. An HTML report can be opened in a browser; the editable source ends in
`.Rmd` and should be kept too.

These course webpages are built with Quarto. Your reports use R Markdown. You do
not need to create a Quarto document or learn a second report system.

## Open the supplied template

Open the project and then `report.Rmd` from its root folder. First save an
unchanged backup if you want one. Keep your working `.Rmd` at the project root so
that `data/seedlings.csv` points to the supplied data. Moving it into `reports/`
would change the relative location of the data during an ordinary knit.

The template has a short header between `---` lines, including a title and
`output: html_document`. That header configures the document. Leave the output
format unchanged for now. A heading in ordinary text starts with `#`, while a
code comment starting with `#` lives inside a code chunk. Their location matters.

Here is a minimal complete report. The three-backtick fences in the box belong
in your `.Rmd` file.

<pre><code>---
title: "Seedling growth"
output: html_document
---

## Question

How much did the seedlings grow during the observation period?

&#96;&#96;&#96;{r import}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
seedlings &lt;- read_csv("data/seedlings.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
seedlings &lt;- mutate(seedlings, growth_mm = final_mm - initial_mm)
&#96;&#96;&#96;

There are &#96;r nrow(seedlings)&#96; plants in the dataset.

&#96;&#96;&#96;{r mean-growth}
mean(seedlings$growth_mm)
&#96;&#96;&#96;

Growth is final minus initial length, measured in millimetres.
</code></pre>

The fences mark where an R **chunk** starts and ends. Chunk labels such as `import` are names
for sections of code and must be unique within a report. The inline expression
in the sentence inserts a calculated result into prose; R executes it during
rendering. You can begin with ordinary prose and add inline calculations later.

## Render, rather than assembling results by hand

Save the source, then choose **Knit**. Rendering runs the chunks in document
order and creates an HTML file. For an explicit equivalent command from the R
Console, use the following command. Do not put it inside `report.Rmd`: a report
must not try to render itself.

```{r}
rmarkdown::render("report.Rmd", output_dir = "reports")
```

`rmarkdown::render` calls a function in the `rmarkdown` package without loading
all of that package's functions. Its `output_dir` puts the rendered result in
`reports/`; the `.Rmd` stays at the project root. The Knit button may initially
put its HTML next to the source instead. Both are HTML reports; locate the
actual file rather than assuming it appeared in a particular folder.

A report must contain its imports and calculations. An object you created only
in the Console may let a chunk run interactively, yet be absent during knitting.
The saved source must be sufficient to rebuild the result from the saved data.

## Add a figure and its meaning

In your report, load `ggplot2` and reuse the growth plot from day 8. Give the
figure a caption by starting its chunk with this line:

<pre><code>&#96;&#96;&#96;{r growth-figure, fig.cap="Each point represents one independently potted seedling."}
# Put the plotting code here.
&#96;&#96;&#96;
</code></pre>

Replace the comment with the plotting code, keeping both chunk fences. Write a sentence below the figure
explaining what the vertical axis measures. A caption identifies what a figure
shows; the surrounding text explains why it matters. Code can be visible in this
first report so that your method is easy to inspect.

## Your practical

1. Render the supplied template before changing it. Confirm the HTML opens.
2. Change its title, question, and author information; save and render again.
3. Put the import, growth calculation, and labelled plot in chunks in the right
   order. Remove repeated chunks that create the same object unnecessarily.
4. Add methods explaining what one row represents and how growth was calculated.
5. Deliberately misspell a column name, render, and read the error's chunk name.
   Fix the spelling and render successfully. Practise recovery, not memorisation.
6. Restart R and render the document again using the command above.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hint: rendering stops

Read the first useful error and its chunk label. Check that the document loads
packages before using their functions, imports the data before calculating, and
uses the exact filename and column names. Check every chunk has an opening and
closing fence. Ask for help with the error text; never attach passwords.
:::

## Check your understanding

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Which files do you keep?

Keep the `.Rmd` source, its input data, and the generated HTML. HTML is convenient
for reading; it does not replace the source needed to update the analysis.
Changing a number in the prose by hand would break the link to its calculation.
:::

**Keep:** your saved `report.Rmd` and a successfully rendered HTML report.
